subproblems.title: The zero current is integer multiplicity
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ and every set U ⊆ ℝ^P, the zero current 0 ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n, whose value on every test form is 0) is integer multiplicity: some IMRep R of the contract (structure IMRep U n) represents it, i.e. 0 = R.action ω for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)), IsIntegerMultiplicity (0 : GeometricCurrentOn U n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent's supplied proof ("The zero current (in every degree) is integer multiplicity: the IMRep with empty carrier, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 represents it"). Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n]; IsIntegerMultiplicity X means ∃ R : IMRep U n, R.Represents X, and R.Represents X means X ω = R.action ω for every ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, where R.action ω = ∫_{x ∈ R.carrier} (R.mult x : ℝ) · R.orient x (ω x) dHⁿ.

1. (The triple.) Let R have carrier ∅, multiplicity mult := (fun _ => 0) and orientation orient := (fun _ => 0). We check the eight proof fields of the structure IMRep U n.
   (a) measurableSet_carrier: MeasurableSet ∅ (MeasurableSet.empty).
   (b) carrier_subset: ∅ ⊆ U (Set.empty_subset).
   (c) rectifiable: Hⁿ(∅) = 0 (measure_empty), hence CountablyRectifiable n ∅ by Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero.
   (d) measurable_mult: a constant map is measurable (measurable_const).
   (e) mult_pos: the hypothesis x ∈ ∅ is impossible.
   (f) locallyIntegrable_mult: for every K, ∅ ∩ K = ∅ (Set.empty_inter) and Hⁿ restricted to ∅ is the zero measure (Measure.restrict_empty), so ∫⁻_{∅ ∩ K} (mult x : [0, ∞]) dHⁿ = 0 (lintegral_zero_measure), which is ≠ ∞.
   (g) aestronglyMeasurable_orient: a constant function is a.e. strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_const).
   (h) orients: Hⁿ⌞∅ = 0 (Measure.restrict_empty), and every property holds almost everywhere for the zero measure (ae_zero: the a.e. filter of 0 is ⊥, so any ∀ᵐ statement is true).
2. (R represents 0.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). The zero current takes the value 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.zero_apply). The action is R.action ω = ∫_{x ∈ ∅} 0 · 0 dHⁿ, an integral with respect to Hⁿ⌞∅ = 0, hence 0 (Measure.restrict_empty, integral_zero_measure). So (0 : GeometricCurrentOn U n) ω = R.action ω.
3. (Conclusion.) By step 2, R.Represents 0, so IsIntegerMultiplicity (0 : GeometricCurrentOn U n) holds with witness R. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take the IMRep with carrier ∅, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0; all fields hold because Hⁿ⌞∅ = 0 and ∅ is countably rectifiable (Hⁿ(∅) = 0).
Its action is an integral with respect to Hⁿ⌞∅ = 0, hence equals 0, the value of the zero current; so it represents 0.

subproblems.title: Support calculus on ℝ^P: vanishing off a closed set, closedness, differences, zero current, boundary
subproblems.statement: Support calculus for currents on all of ℝ^P (domain U = univ). Let P, n ∈ ℕ. (i) If E ⊆ ℝ^P is closed and X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) satisfies X(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) whose tsupport is disjoint from E, then spt X ⊆ E. (ii) spt X is closed for every X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P). (iii) spt(A − B) ⊆ spt A ∪ spt B for all A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P). (iv) The zero current 0 ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) has empty support. (v) spt ∂A ⊆ spt A for every A ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P). Here spt X = X.support = univ \ X.zeroRegion, where X.zeroRegion is the union of all open W ⊆ ℝ^P with compact closure (closure W ⊆ univ) on which X vanishes, i.e. X(ω) = 0 for every ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W (GeometricCurrentOn.VanishesOn), and A − B, 0, ∂A are the contract subtraction, the zero current and the boundary (∂A(η) = A(dη)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), (∀ (E : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), IsClosed E → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) E → X ω = 0) → X.support ⊆ E) ∧ (∀ X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, IsClosed X.support) ∧ (∀ A B : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, (A - B).support ⊆ A.support ∪ B.support) ∧ (0 : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n).support = ∅ ∧ (∀ A : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (n + 1), A.boundary.support ⊆ A.support)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the support facts listed in the notation paragraph of the parent's supplied proof ("spt(A − B) ⊆ spt A ∪ spt B; spt ∂A ⊆ spt A; spt 0 = ∅; a current that vanishes on every test form whose support is disjoint from a closed set E has support in E (every x ∉ E has a ball with compact closure disjoint from E)"), proved directly from Simon's definition 6.2.11 (no use of the partition-of-unity fact (VO) is needed).

Notation: for X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), x ∉ spt X ⟺ x ∈ X.zeroRegion ⟺ there is W with x ∈ W, W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ univ, and X.VanishesOn W (∀ ω, tsupport ω ⊆ W → X(ω) = 0); call such W a zero neighbourhood of x for X. Since ℝ^P is a proper metric space, for every x and ε > 0 the ball W = ball x ε is open with closure W ⊆ closedBall x ε (closure_ball_subset_closedBall), a compact set (isCompact_closedBall), so closure W is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset with isClosed_closure); trivially closure W ⊆ univ.

1. (i) Let E be closed and X vanish on all test forms whose tsupport is disjoint from E. Let x ∈ spt X and suppose x ∉ E. As Eᶜ is open, there is ε > 0 with ball x ε ⊆ Eᶜ (Metric.isOpen_iff). Put W := ball x ε. It is open with compact closure (notation paragraph). If tsupport ω ⊆ W then tsupport ω ⊆ Eᶜ, i.e. Disjoint (tsupport ω) E, so X(ω) = 0 by hypothesis. Hence W is a zero neighbourhood of x and x ∈ X.zeroRegion, contradicting x ∈ spt X. Therefore x ∈ E, i.e. spt X ⊆ E.
2. (ii) spt X = univ \ X.zeroRegion = (X.zeroRegion)ᶜ and X.zeroRegion is open, being a union of open sets (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion). Hence spt X is closed (IsOpen.isClosed_compl).
3. (iii) Let x ∉ spt A ∪ spt B, with zero neighbourhoods W_A of x for A and W_B of x for B. Put W := W_A ∩ W_B: it is open and contains x; closure W ⊆ closure W_A (closure_mono), so closure W is a closed subset of a compact set, hence compact; closure W ⊆ univ. If tsupport ω ⊆ W, then tsupport ω ⊆ W_A and tsupport ω ⊆ W_B, so A(ω) = 0 and B(ω) = 0, and (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω) = 0. So W is a zero neighbourhood of x for A − B, and x ∉ spt(A − B). Contrapositively spt(A − B) ⊆ spt A ∪ spt B.
4. (iv) For every x, W := ball x 1 is open with compact closure, and the zero current vanishes on every test form (GeometricCurrentOn.zero_apply), in particular on W. So every x lies in the zero region of 0, and spt 0 = ∅.
5. (v) Let A ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) and x ∉ spt A, with a zero neighbourhood W of x for A. Let η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport η ⊆ W. Then ∂A(η) = A(dη) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply), where the form underlying dη is exteriorDerivative η and tsupport (exteriorDerivative η) ⊆ tsupport η ⊆ W (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset). Hence A(dη) = 0, i.e. ∂A vanishes on W, W is a zero neighbourhood of x for ∂A, and x ∉ spt ∂A. So spt ∂A ⊆ spt A. ∎
proof_key_steps: Points off spt X are exactly the points with an open neighbourhood of compact closure on which X vanishes; small balls are such neighbourhoods in the proper space ℝ^P.
(i) For x ∉ E (closed), a ball around x inside Eᶜ is a zero neighbourhood, so spt X ⊆ E; (ii) spt X is the complement of the open zero region.
(iii) Intersect zero neighbourhoods of A and B; (iv) every ball is a zero neighbourhood of 0; (v) tsupport dη ⊆ tsupport η, so zero neighbourhoods of A are zero neighbourhoods of ∂A.

subproblems.title: Mass of an integral current: M_V(ω ↦ ∫_E ξ(ω) dμ) ≤ μ(E ∩ V) when |ξ| ≤ 1 a.e.
subproblems.statement: Mass bound for a current given by integration against a measure. Let P, d ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, X ∈ 𝒟_d(U), μ a measure on ℝ^P, ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_d a function with values in d-vectors (MultiVector P d = continuous linear functionals on d-covectors), and E, V ⊆ ℝ^P arbitrary sets. Assume that for μ-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every d-covector α, and that X(ω) = ∫_E ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) (Bochner integral with respect to μ⌞E). Then M_V(X) ≤ μ(E ∩ V) in [0, ∞].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U d) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P d) (E V : Set (Euclid P)), (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) d, |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U d, X ω = ∫ x in E, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) x) ∂μ) → X.massOn V ≤ μ (E ∩ V)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the mass estimates "M(W_j) ≤ μ_T(E_j), M(D_j) ≤ μ_∂(E_j)" of step 6 (6a) of the parent's supplied proof, i.e. Simon (6.2.5) for the current ω ↦ ∫_E ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ with |ξ| ≤ 1. No measurability of E or V and no integrability is needed.

1. (Reduction.) By definition M_V(X) = sSup {ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U d V}. By sSup_le it suffices to show ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) ≤ μ(E ∩ V) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ V and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. Fix such an ω and put g(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)) and S := tsupport ω, a closed (hence measurable) set with S ⊆ V.
2. (Pointwise bound.) Let x be a point where the a.e. hypothesis holds. If x ∈ S then |g(x)| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1. If x ∉ S then ω(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and g(x) = ξ(x)(0) = 0 because ξ(x) is linear. Hence ‖g(x)‖ₑ = ENNReal.ofReal |g(x)| ≤ S.indicator 1 x for μ-a.e. x, and therefore for μ⌞E-a.e. x (ae_restrict_of_ae).
3. (Integral bound.) For every real y, ENNReal.ofReal y ≤ ENNReal.ofReal |y| = ‖y‖ₑ. Hence
   ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) = ENNReal.ofReal ∫ g d(μ⌞E) ≤ ‖∫ g d(μ⌞E)‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻ ‖g‖ₑ d(μ⌞E)
   by enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm (valid for every function: a non-integrable function has Bochner integral 0). By step 2 and lintegral_mono_ae, ∫⁻ ‖g‖ₑ d(μ⌞E) ≤ ∫⁻ S.indicator 1 d(μ⌞E) = (μ⌞E)(S) (lintegral_indicator_one, S measurable) = μ(S ∩ E) (Measure.restrict_apply, S measurable) ≤ μ(E ∩ V) (measure_mono, as S ∩ E ⊆ E ∩ V).
4. (Conclusion.) Every element of the set whose supremum defines M_V(X) is ≤ μ(E ∩ V), so M_V(X) ≤ μ(E ∩ V). ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to one admissible ω (sSup_le).
|ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ 1 on tsupport ω and = 0 off it, for μ-a.e. x.
ofReal X(ω) ≤ ‖∫_E ξ(ω) dμ‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_E ‖ξ(ω)‖ₑ dμ ≤ μ(tsupport ω ∩ E) ≤ μ(E ∩ V).

subproblems.title: Good slicing radius by Lebesgue differentiation and Markov (Simon 6.5.1, (8)–(10))
subproblems.statement: Choice of a good slicing radius (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, displays (8)–(10)). Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ, μ' be finite measures on ℝ^P (IsFiniteMeasure), f : ℝ^P → ℝ measurable, ρ > 0 real and B ∈ [0, ∞] with μ({x : f(x) < ρ}) ≤ B. Then there is r with ρ/2 < r < ρ such that liminf_{h → 0+} h⁻¹·μ({x : r − h < f(x) < r}) ≤ (4/ρ)·B and liminf_{h → 0+} h⁻¹·μ'({x : r − h < f(x) < r}) < ∞. Values are in [0, ∞]: h⁻¹ and 4/ρ are read through ENNReal.ofReal, and liminf is taken along the filter 𝓝[>] 0 of right neighbourhoods of 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ μ' : Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (ρ : ℝ) (B : ℝ≥0∞), IsFiniteMeasure μ → IsFiniteMeasure μ' → Measurable f → 0 < ρ → μ {x | f x < ρ} ≤ B → ∃ r ∈ Ioo (ρ / 2) ρ, liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ {x | r - h < f x ∧ f x < r}) (𝓝[>] 0) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (4 / ρ) * B ∧ liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ' {x | r - h < f x ∧ f x < r}) (𝓝[>] 0) < ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent's supplied proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, (8)–(10): Lebesgue differentiation of t ↦ μ_T({d < t}) and a Markov argument on (ρ_ν/2, ρ_ν)), isolated for general finite measures. Throughout, ofReal := ENNReal.ofReal and λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ (volume).

1. (Distribution functions.) Put F(t) := (μ({f < t})).toReal and G(t) := (μ'({f < t})).toReal. Since μ, μ' are finite, μ({f < t}) = ofReal(F(t)) and μ'({f < t}) = ofReal(G(t)) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal, measure_ne_top). F and G are monotone (measure_mono and ENNReal.toReal_mono) and nonnegative. The sets {f < t} are measurable because f is (measurableSet_lt).
2. (Slice bound.) Let t ∈ ℝ and h > 0. Then {f < t − h} ⊆ {f < t} and {t − h < f < t} ⊆ {f < t} \ {f < t − h}. Hence μ({t − h < f < t}) ≤ μ({f < t}) − μ({f < t − h}) (measure_mono, measure_sdiff with finite measure) = ofReal(F(t)) − ofReal(F(t − h)) = ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)) (ENNReal.ofReal_sub, F(t − h) ≥ 0). Multiplying by ofReal(h⁻¹) and using ofReal(a)·ofReal(b) = ofReal(a·b) for a ≥ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_mul): ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ({t − h < f < t}) ≤ ofReal((F(t) − F(t − h))/h). The same holds for μ' and G.
3. (Derivative bound.) If F is differentiable at t, then liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ({t − h < f < t}) ≤ ofReal(deriv F t). Indeed, HasDerivAt F (deriv F t) t gives s⁻¹(F(t + s) − F(t)) → deriv F t as s → 0 with s < 0 (HasDerivAt.tendsto_slope_zero_left). The map h ↦ −h sends the filter 𝓝[>] 0 into 𝓝[<] 0, and for s = −h we have s⁻¹(F(t + s) − F(t)) = (F(t) − F(t − h))/h. Hence (F(t) − F(t − h))/h → deriv F t as h → 0+, and by continuity of ofReal, ofReal((F(t) − F(t − h))/h) → ofReal(deriv F t), so the liminf of this function equals ofReal(deriv F t) (Tendsto.liminf_eq; the filter is not trivial). subproblems.title: Componentwise McShane extension into ℝ^P with constant √P·K
subproblems.statement: Lipschitz extension into Euclidean space (componentwise McShane). Let P ∈ ℕ, S ⊆ ℝ^P, ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P and K ∈ ℝ≥0 such that ψ is K-Lipschitz on S (LipschitzOnWith K ψ S: ‖ψ(x) − ψ(y)‖ ≤ K‖x − y‖ for x, y ∈ S). Then there is φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P which is (√P·K)-Lipschitz on all of ℝ^P (LipschitzWith (NNReal.sqrt P * K) φ, where P is cast to ℝ≥0) and agrees with ψ on S (EqOn φ ψ S).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent's supplied proof ("φ_r is the componentwise McShane extension of ψ|{d ≥ r} (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real for each coordinate x ↦ ψ(x)_i ...). Then φ_r : ℝ^P → ℝ^P is (√P c_R/r)-Lipschitz and φ_r = ψ on {d ≥ r}"), for an arbitrary set S and constant K. Coordinates: for v ∈ ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) write v_i := v i; then ‖v‖² = Σ_i v_i² and dist(v, w)² = Σ_i (v_i − w_i)² (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, EuclideanSpace.dist_eq).

1. (Coordinates are K-Lipschitz on S.) Fix i ∈ Fin P and put ψ_i(x) := ψ(x)_i. For x, y ∈ S, |ψ_i(x) − ψ_i(y)| = |(ψ(x) − ψ(y))_i| ≤ ‖ψ(x) − ψ(y)‖ ≤ K·dist(x, y), because a single coordinate is bounded by the Euclidean norm (v_i² ≤ Σ_j v_j²). So ψ_i is LipschitzOnWith K on S (LipschitzOnWith.of_dist_le_mul).
2. (McShane.) By LipschitzOnWith.extend_real there is g_i : ℝ^P → ℝ which is K-Lipschitz on ℝ^P and equals ψ_i on S. Choose such g_i for every i (finitely many).
3. (Definition.) Let φ(x) ∈ ℝ^P be the vector with coordinates φ(x)_i = g_i(x) (the EuclideanSpace vector of the function i ↦ g_i(x), e.g. WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => g_i x) / (EuclideanSpace.equiv _ _).symm).
4. (Lipschitz constant.) For x, y ∈ ℝ^P, dist(φ(x), φ(y))² = Σ_i (g_i(x) − g_i(y))² ≤ Σ_i K²·dist(x, y)² = P·K²·dist(x, y)². Taking square roots (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt, √(P K² D²) = √P·K·D for K, D ≥ 0), dist(φ(x), φ(y)) ≤ √P·K·dist(x, y). Since the real number underlying NNReal.sqrt P * K is √P·K (Real.coe_sqrt, NNReal.coe_natCast), φ is LipschitzWith (NNReal.sqrt P * K) (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul).
5. (Agreement on S.) For x ∈ S and every i, φ(x)_i = g_i(x) = ψ_i(x) = ψ(x)_i, so φ(x) = ψ(x) (equality of coordinates). Hence EqOn φ ψ S. ∎
proof_key_steps: Each coordinate ψ_i is K-Lipschitz on S (a coordinate is bounded by the Euclidean norm).
Extend each ψ_i to a K-Lipschitz g_i on ℝ^P (LipschitzOnWith.extend_real) and set φ(x) := (g_i(x))_i.
dist(φ x, φ y)² = Σ_i (g_i x − g_i y)² ≤ P K² dist(x, y)², so φ is √P·K-Lipschitz; φ = ψ on S coordinatewise.

Source: steps 2, 5 and 6 of the parent's supplied proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, displays (8)–(10), chapter-06.txt lines 1405–1928, with the shells of the parent's E3). Here the density bounds, which the parent obtains from the good centre, are hypotheses, and the shells are taken half-open. Siblings used: S = cmcsd_support_calculus, ML = cmcsd_massOn_le_measure_inter, GR = cmcsd_good_radius, IR = lcmp_imRep_measure_restrict, MS = cmc_fc_cs_massOn_sub_le (M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B)), EB = cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn (|X(ω)| ≤ c·M_W(X).toReal if M_W(X) ≠ ∞, tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ c).

Notation. n := m + 1; all currents are on univ = ℝ^P, which is open; M(X) = M_{ℝ^P}(X). d is continuous, so {d < t} is open, {d ≥ t} and {d = t} are closed, and all are Borel. ρ_j := (1/2)^{j+2}, so 0 < ρ_j ≤ 1/4, ρ_j/2 = (1/2)^{j+3} and ρ_j → 0. For a test form ω let c_ω := sup_x |ω(x)| < ∞: x ↦ |ω(x)| is continuous (covectorEuclideanNorm is the square root of a finite sum of squares of continuous evaluation maps) and vanishes outside the compact set tsupport ω (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support).

1. (The mass measure of T.) Choose an IMRep R representing T and put μ_T := R.measure, ξ := R.orient.
   (1a) By (MR) (U = ℝ^P open), M_W(T) = μ_T(W) for every open W; in particular μ_T(ℝ^P) = M(T) < ∞, so μ_T is a finite measure and is finite on compact sets.
   (1b) By IR (a), (b), μ_T ≪ Hⁿ⌞R.carrier and ξ is μ_T-a.e. strongly measurable. By (IMC)(d), |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α for Hⁿ⌞R.carrier-a.e. x, hence for μ_T-a.e. x (absolute continuity, AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le).
   (1c) By IR (c) with E := ℝ^P and R′ := R (R.carrier = R.carrier ∩ ℝ^P), R.action ω = ∫_{ℝ^P} ξ(ω) dμ_T = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ_T(x) (Measure.restrict_univ); since R represents T, T(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ_T for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ.
   (1d) μ_T(ℝ^P \ spt T) = 0. Indeed spt T is closed (S (ii)), so G := ℝ^P \ spt T is open and μ_T(G) = M_G(T) by (1a); every ω admissible for M_G has tsupport ω ⊆ G, i.e. disjoint from spt T, so T(ω) = 0 by (VO); hence M_G(T) is the supremum of a set contained in {0}, i.e. 0.
2. (A measure for ∂T.) For every W, M_W(∂T) ≤ M(∂T) < ∞ (massOn_mono). So (REP) with U := ℝ^P and the current ∂T ∈ 𝒟_m gives a measure μ_∂ and ξ_∂ : ℝ^P → Λ_m with: μ_∂ finite on compact sets; M_W(∂T) = μ_∂(W) for open W, so μ_∂(ℝ^P) = M(∂T) < ∞ and μ_∂ is finite; ξ_∂ is μ_∂-a.e. strongly measurable; |ξ_∂(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x and α; ∂T(η) = ∫ ξ_∂(η) dμ_∂ for every η ∈ 𝒟^m. Exactly as in (1d) (S (ii), (VO)), μ_∂(ℝ^P \ spt ∂T) = 0.
3. (Integrability.) For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ, x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ_T-a.e. strongly measurable (image of the a.e. strongly measurable pair (ξ, ω) under the continuous evaluation map (L, α) ↦ L(α)) and bounded by c_ω for μ_T-a.e. x (1b), hence μ_T-integrable (Integrable.of_bound, μ_T finite), and integrable on every subset. Likewise x ↦ ξ_∂(x)(η(x)) is μ_∂-integrable for η ∈ 𝒟^m.
4. (Slicing by d.) Apply (SL) with k := m, U := ℝ^P, T, μ := μ_T, μ' := μ_∂, ξ, ξ' := ξ_∂, f := d, L := 1 (its hypotheses are (1a)–(1c), step 2 and LipschitzWith 1 d; the a.e. bound for ξ_∂ holds everywhere). It gives A : ℝ → 𝒟_n, B : ℝ → 𝒟_m with
   (SL1) A_t(ω) = ∫_{{d<t}} ξ(ω) dμ_T; (SL2) B_t(η) = ∫_{{d<t}} ξ_∂(η) dμ_∂;
   (SL3) ∂A_t(η) = B_t(η) whenever tsupport η is disjoint from {d = t};
   (SL4) for W := ℝ^P (open; ℝ^P ∩ S = S): M(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ 1·liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ_T({t − h < d < t}).
5. (Good radii.) Fix j. Put β_j := C·ofReal(ρ_j^{m+2})·M(T). Since {d < ρ_j} is open, μ_T({d < ρ_j}) = M_{{d<ρ_j}}(T) ≤ β_j by (1a) and the density hypothesis (0 < ρ_j ≤ 1/4). d is measurable (continuous) and μ_T, μ_∂ are finite, so GR (with μ := μ_T, μ' := μ_∂, f := d, ρ := ρ_j, B := β_j) gives r_j with ρ_j/2 < r_j < ρ_j and
   (5a) liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ_T({r_j − h < d < r_j}) ≤ ofReal(4/ρ_j)·β_j = 4C·ofReal(ρ_j^{m+1})·M(T) (ofReal(4/ρ)·ofReal(ρ^{m+2}) = ofReal(4ρ^{m+1}) = 4·ofReal(ρ^{m+1}) for ρ > 0);
   (5b) liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ_∂({r_j − h < d < r_j}) < ∞.
   Choose such r_j for every j (choice). Then (1/2)^{j+3} < r_j < (1/2)^{j+2} (first conclusion), and r_{j+1} < ρ_{j+1} = ρ_j/2 < r_j, so the r_j strictly decrease.
6. (Definitions.) W_0 := T − A_{r_0}, W_{j+1} := A_{r_j} − A_{r_{j+1}}; D_0 := ∂T − B_{r_0}, D_{j+1} := B_{r_j} − B_{r_{j+1}}; Z_j := ∂A_{r_j} − B_{r_j}. Shells: E_0 := {d ≥ r_0}, E_{j+1} := {r_{j+1} ≤ d < r_j}. They are Borel and pairwise disjoint (the r_j decrease), and E_j ⊆ {d ≥ r_j}.
7. (Integral formulas.) For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ, η ∈ 𝒟^m and all j: W_j(ω) = ∫_{E_j} ξ(ω) dμ_T and D_j(η) = ∫_{E_j} ξ_∂(η) dμ_∂. For j = 0: by (1c), (SL1), {d < r_0}ᶜ = E_0 and integral_add_compl (integrability, step 3), T(ω) − A_{r_0}(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ_T − ∫_{{d<r_0}} ξ(ω) dμ_T = ∫_{E_0} ξ(ω) dμ_T. For j + 1: {d < r_{j+1}} ⊆ {d < r_j} and {d < r_j} \ {d < r_{j+1}} = E_{j+1}, so ∫_{{d<r_j}} − ∫_{{d<r_{j+1}}} = ∫_{E_{j+1}} (setIntegral_sdiff, step 3). The same computations with step 2, (SL2) give the formulas for D_j.
8. (W_j is integer multiplicity.) (IMC)(b) with U := ℝ^P, R and the Borel set E_j gives a current W′_j and an IMRep R′_j representing W′_j with carrier R.carrier ∩ E_j, multiplicity R.mult and orientation R.orient. By IR (c), R′_j.action ω = ∫_{E_j} ξ(ω) dμ_T = W_j(ω) (step 7). Hence W′_j(ω) = W_j(ω) for every ω, so W′_j = W_j (GeometricCurrentOn.ext) and W_j is IM.
9. (Boundary relations.) For η ∈ 𝒟^m (pointwise identities; then GeometricCurrentOn.ext): ∂W_0(η) = T(dη) − A_{r_0}(dη) = ∂T(η) − ∂A_{r_0}(η) = (∂T(η) − B_{r_0}(η)) − (∂A_{r_0}(η) − B_{r_0}(η)) = D_0(η) − Z_0(η); and ∂W_{j+1}(η) = ∂A_{r_j}(η) − ∂A_{r_{j+1}}(η) = (B_{r_j}(η) − B_{r_{j+1}}(η)) − ((∂A_{r_{j+1}}(η) − B_{r_{j+1}}(η)) − (∂A_{r_j}(η) − B_{r_j}(η))) = D_{j+1}(η) − (Z_{j+1}(η) − Z_j(η)). So ∂W_0 = D_0 − Z_0 and ∂W_{j+1} = D_{j+1} − (Z_{j+1} − Z_j).
10. (Supports.)
   (10a) K_j := spt T ∩ {d ≥ r_j} is closed (S (ii); d continuous). Let tsupport ω be disjoint from K_j. For x ∈ E_j ∩ spt T we have x ∈ K_j, so x ∉ tsupport ω, ω(x) = 0 and ξ(x)(ω(x)) = 0; since μ_T(ℝ^P \ spt T) = 0 (1d), the integrand of step 7 vanishes μ_T-a.e. on E_j, so W_j(ω) = 0 (integral_eq_zero_of_ae). By S (i), spt W_j ⊆ spt T ∩ {d ≥ r_j}.
   (10b) In the same way, using step 7 for D_j and μ_∂(ℝ^P \ spt ∂T) = 0 (step 2), spt D_j ⊆ spt ∂T ∩ {d ≥ r_j}.
   (10c) If tsupport η is disjoint from the closed set {d = r_j}, then Z_j(η) = ∂A_{r_j}(η) − B_{r_j}(η) = 0 by (SL3); so spt Z_j ⊆ {d = r_j} (S (i)). If tsupport η is disjoint from spt T, then ∂A_{r_j}(η) = A_{r_j}(dη) = ∫_{{d<r_j}} ξ(dη) dμ_T = 0, because the form underlying dη vanishes outside tsupport(dη) ⊆ tsupport η (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), hence on spt T, and μ_T(ℝ^P \ spt T) = 0; and B_{r_j}(η) = ∫_{{d<r_j}} ξ_∂(η) dμ_∂ = 0, because η vanishes on spt T ⊇ spt ∂T (S (v)) and μ_∂(ℝ^P \ spt ∂T) = 0. Hence Z_j(η) = 0 and spt Z_j ⊆ spt T (S (i)). Together spt Z_j ⊆ spt T ∩ {d = r_j}.
   (10d) spt ∂T ⊆ spt T (S (v)). Each of spt W_j, spt D_j, spt Z_j is closed (S (ii)) and contained in the compact set spt T, hence compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset).
11. (Masses.) By ML (a.e. bounds (1b) and step 2; formulas of step 7 and (SL1)), M(W_j) ≤ μ_T(E_j), M(D_j) ≤ μ_∂(E_j) and M(A_t) ≤ μ_T({d < t}).
   (11a) M(W_0) ≤ μ_T(ℝ^P) = M(T) and M(D_0) ≤ μ_∂(ℝ^P) = M(∂T).
   (11b) E_{j+1} ⊆ {d < r_j} ⊆ {d < ρ_j}, so M(W_{j+1}) ≤ μ_T({d < ρ_j}) = M_{{d<ρ_j}}(T) ≤ C·ofReal(ρ_j^{m+2})·M(T) = C·ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)})·M(T) (density hypothesis with r := ρ_j; ρ_j^{m+2} = (1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)} by pow_mul), and likewise M(D_{j+1}) ≤ μ_∂({d < ρ_j}) = M_{{d<ρ_j}}(∂T) ≤ C·ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)})·M(∂T).
   (11c) By (SL4) and (5a), M(Z_j) ≤ 4C·ofReal(ρ_j^{m+1})·M(T) = 4C·ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+1)})·M(T).
   All these bounds are finite (C, the ofReal values, M(T) and M(∂T) are finite).
12. (Boundary masses.)
   (12a) By step 9 and MS, M(∂W_0) ≤ M(D_0) + M(Z_0) and M(∂W_{j+1}) ≤ M(D_{j+1}) + M(Z_{j+1}) + M(Z_j), finite by step 11.
   (12b) If m = 0, boundaryMassOn D_j ℝ^P = boundaryMassOn Z_j ℝ^P = 0 by definition. Let m = k + 1. Apply (SL) a second time with k, U := ℝ^P, the current ∂T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}, μ := μ_∂, μ' := 0 (the zero measure), ξ := ξ_∂, ξ' := 0, f := d, L := 1. Its hypotheses hold: μ_∂ and 0 are finite on compacts; ξ_∂ and 0 are a.e. strongly measurable and satisfy the a.e. bounds (step 2; trivially for the zero measure); ∂T(η) = ∫ ξ_∂(η) dμ_∂ (step 2); ∂(∂T) = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary) and ∫ 0 d0 = 0 (integral_zero_measure). It yields A′, B′ with A′_t(η) = ∫_{{d<t}} ξ_∂(η) dμ_∂ = B_t(η), so A′_t = B_t (ext), and B′_t(ζ) = ∫_{{d<t}} 0 d0 = 0, so B′_t = 0, and M(∂A′_t − B′_t) ≤ liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ_∂({t − h < d < t}). As ∂A′_t − B′_t = ∂B_t (ext: ∂B_t(ζ) − 0 = ∂B_t(ζ)), (5b) gives M(∂B_{r_j}) < ∞ for every j. Using (X − Y).boundary = ∂X − ∂Y (ext), ∂∂ = 0, M(0) = 0 and MS: ∂D_0 = ∂∂T − ∂B_{r_0} = 0 − ∂B_{r_0}, ∂D_{j+1} = ∂B_{r_j} − ∂B_{r_{j+1}} and ∂Z_j = ∂∂A_{r_j} − ∂B_{r_j} = 0 − ∂B_{r_j} have finite mass. For degree k + 1, boundaryMassOn X ℝ^P = M(∂X) by definition, which proves the claim.
13. (Σ_j W_j(ω) = T(ω).) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ. (i) Absolute convergence: by EB (W := ℝ^P, c := c_ω) and step 11, |W_j(ω)| ≤ c_ω·M(W_j).toReal ≤ c_ω·μ_T(E_j).toReal; the E_j are pairwise disjoint Borel sets, so Σ_j μ_T(E_j) = μ_T(⋃_j E_j) ≤ μ_T(ℝ^P) < ∞ (measure_iUnion); hence Σ_j |W_j(ω)| < ∞ (ENNReal.summable_toReal) and (W_j(ω))_j is summable (Summable.of_norm_bounded). (ii) Partial sums: by induction on N, Σ_{j=0}^{N} W_j(ω) = T(ω) − A_{r_N}(ω), because W_0(ω) = T(ω) − A_{r_0}(ω) and W_{N+1}(ω) = A_{r_N}(ω) − A_{r_{N+1}}(ω). (iii) M(A_{r_N}) ≤ μ_T({d < r_N}) ≤ μ_T({d < ρ_N}) ≤ C·ofReal(ρ_N^{m+2})·M(T) → 0 as N → ∞ (ρ_N → 0, M(T) < ∞; ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul), so by EB |A_{r_N}(ω)| ≤ c_ω·M(A_{r_N}).toReal → 0. Hence the partial sums tend to T(ω), and by (i) HasSum (j ↦ W_j(ω)) (T(ω)) (Summable.hasSum_iff_tendsto_nat).
14. (Conclusion.) The radii r_j (step 5) and the currents W_j, D_j, Z_j (step 6) satisfy: the radius bounds (step 5); HasSum (step 13); the boundary relations (step 9); integrality of W_j (step 8); compactness of supports (10d), finiteness of M(W_j), M(D_j), M(Z_j) (step 11), of M(∂W_j) (12a) and of boundaryMassOn D_j ℝ^P, boundaryMassOn Z_j ℝ^P (12b); the support inclusions (10a)–(10c); and the mass bounds (11a)–(11c). ∎

Assume, as a hypothesis of the statement, (VO): the frozen type of Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support (S(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω is disjoint from spt S). Let P, m ∈ ℕ and let push_k(F, X) ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P), homot_k(F, G, X) ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) be operations (k ∈ ℕ, F, G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P, X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P), domain univ) satisfying (PF), the conclusion of the frozen type of the parent's sibling Submission.cmcdt_lipschitz_pushforward_homotopy for this P (taken verbatim as a hypothesis): calling X normal with compact support (NC) when spt X is compact, M(X) < ∞ and boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞ (= M(∂X) for k ≥ 1, 0 for k = 0), for all Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, all Λ-Lipschitz F, G, F', G' and all NC X, Y of degree k: (1) push_k(id, X) = X; (2) push_k(F, X − Y) = push_k(F, X) − push_k(F, Y) and homot_k(F, G, X − Y) = homot_k(F, G, X) − homot_k(F, G, Y); (3) if F = F' and G = G' on spt X then push_k(F, X) = push_k(F', X) and homot_k(F, G, X) = homot_k(F', G', X); (4) M(push_k(F, X)) ≤ Λ^k M(X), spt push_k(F, X) ⊆ F(spt X), M(homot_k(F, G, X)) ≤ δ(2Λ)^k M(X) whenever δ ∈ ℝ and |F(x) − G(x)| ≤ δ for x ∈ spt X, and spt homot_k(F, G, X) ⊆ {F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)) : x ∈ spt X, t ∈ [0, 1]}; (5) for X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) with compact support, M(X) < ∞, M(∂X) < ∞: ∂ push_{k+1}(F, X) = push_k(F, ∂X), push_{k+1}(G, X) − push_{k+1}(F, X) − homot_k(F, G, ∂X) = ∂ homot_{k+1}(F, G, X), and if X is integer multiplicity then push_{k+1}(F, X) and homot_{k+1}(F, G, X) are integer multiplicity; (6) for X ∈ 𝒟_0(ℝ^P) with compact support and finite mass, push_0(G, X) − push_0(F, X) = ∂ homot_0(F, G, X). Source: steps 7–9 of the parent's supplied proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, displays (11)–(25), chapter-06.txt lines 1405–1928), with the homotopy taken from φ_j to the identity (F := φ_j, G := id in (PF)), so that the homotopy currents enter with the sign needed for T − Q₀ − S₁ = ∂R₁ and no negation of currents is required. Siblings used: S = cmcsd_support_calculus, MS = cmc_fc_cs_massOn_sub_le, EB = cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn.

Notation. All currents are on univ = ℝ^P; M(X) = M_{ℝ^P}(X); id := (x ↦ x). PF1, …, PF6 are the six conjuncts of (PF): PF1 push_k(id, X) = X; PF2 linearity of push_k(F, ·) and homot_k(F, G, ·) on differences; PF3 locality; PF4 mass bounds M(push_k(F, X)) ≤ Λ^k M(X) and M(homot_k(F, G, X)) ≤ δ'(2Λ)^k M(X) when dist(F x, G x) ≤ δ' on spt X, and support bounds spt push_k(F, X) ⊆ F(spt X), spt homot_k(F, G, X) ⊆ {F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)) : x ∈ spt X, t ∈ [0, 1]}; PF5 for X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1} with compact support, M(X), M(∂X) < ∞: ∂push_{k+1}(F, X) = push_k(F, ∂X), push_{k+1}(G, X) − push_{k+1}(F, X) − homot_k(F, G, ∂X) = ∂homot_{k+1}(F, G, X), and integrality of push_{k+1}(F, X), homot_{k+1}(F, G, X) for IM X (PF6 is not used). PF1–PF4 require X (and Y) to be NC_k: compact support, finite mass and boundaryMassOn X ℝ^P < ∞; maps must be Λ-Lipschitz for one common Λ. For a test form ω, c_ω := sup_x |ω(x)| < ∞ (x ↦ |ω(x)| is continuous and vanishes outside the compact tsupport ω), and dω denotes the exterior-derivative test form, so ∂X(ω) = X(dω).

0. (Preliminaries.)
   (0a) φ_j is Λ_j- and Λ_{j+1}-Lipschitz (Λ_j ≤ Λ_{j+1}, LipschitzWith.weaken); id is 1-Lipschitz, hence Λ_j- and Λ_{j+1}-Lipschitz (1 ≤ Λ_j ≤ Λ_{j+1}).
   (0b) W_j ∈ NC_{m+1} (for degree m + 1, boundaryMassOn W_j ℝ^P = M(∂W_j) by definition); D_j, Z_j ∈ NC_m (hypotheses).
   (0c) Z_{j+1} − Z_j ∈ NC_m: spt(Z_{j+1} − Z_j) ⊆ spt Z_{j+1} ∪ spt Z_j (S (iii)), a compact set, and spt(Z_{j+1} − Z_j) is closed (S (ii)), hence compact; M(Z_{j+1} − Z_j) ≤ M(Z_{j+1}) + M(Z_j) < ∞ (MS); for m = 0 boundaryMassOn of a 0-current is 0, and for m ≥ 1, ∂(Z_{j+1} − Z_j) = ∂Z_{j+1} − ∂Z_j (ext), so its mass is ≤ M(∂Z_{j+1}) + M(∂Z_j) < ∞ (MS).
   (0d) (Evaluation.) If M(X) < ∞ then |X(ω)| ≤ c_ω·M(X).toReal (EB with W := ℝ^P, tsupport ω ⊆ ℝ^P). Hence M(X_N) → 0 implies X_N(ω) → 0 (ENNReal.toReal is continuous at 0), and Σ_j M(X_j) < ∞ implies Σ_j |X_j(ω)| < ∞ (ENNReal.summable_toReal), so (X_j(ω))_j is summable (Summable.of_norm_bounded).
1. (Deformed pieces.) V_j := push_{m+1}(φ_j, W_j), H_j := homot_{m+1}(φ_j, id, W_j) ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}, Y_j := push_m(φ_j, D_j), E′_j := homot_m(φ_j, id, D_j) ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}, L′_j := push_m(φ_j, Z_j), K_j := homot_m(φ_j, id, Z_j) ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}.
2. (Locality.) PF3 with Λ := Λ_{j+1}, F := φ_{j+1}, G := id, F' := φ_j, G' := id (all Λ_{j+1}-Lipschitz by (0a)), X := Z_j ∈ NC_m and φ_{j+1} = φ_j on spt Z_j (hypothesis), id = id: push_m(φ_{j+1}, Z_j) = L′_j and homot_m(φ_{j+1}, id, Z_j) = K_j.
3. (Deforming the boundaries.) PF2 with Λ := Λ_0, F := φ_0, G := id and ∂W_0 = D_0 − Z_0 (D_0, Z_0 ∈ NC_m): push_m(φ_0, ∂W_0) = Y_0 − L′_0 and homot_m(φ_0, id, ∂W_0) = E′_0 − K_0. PF2 with Λ := Λ_{j+1}, F := φ_{j+1}, G := id, applied to ∂W_{j+1} = D_{j+1} − (Z_{j+1} − Z_j) (D_{j+1}, Z_{j+1} − Z_j ∈ NC_m by (0b), (0c)) and then to Z_{j+1} − Z_j (Z_{j+1}, Z_j ∈ NC_m), together with step 2: push_m(φ_{j+1}, ∂W_{j+1}) = Y_{j+1} − (L′_{j+1} − L′_j) and homot_m(φ_{j+1}, id, ∂W_{j+1}) = E′_{j+1} − (K_{j+1} − K_j).
4. (Homotopy formula and integrality.) PF5 with k := m, Λ := Λ_j, F := φ_j, G := id and X := W_j (compact support, M(W_j), M(∂W_j) < ∞) gives
   (4a) ∂V_j = push_m(φ_j, ∂W_j);
   (4b) push_{m+1}(id, W_j) − V_j − homot_m(φ_j, id, ∂W_j) = ∂H_j, and push_{m+1}(id, W_j) = W_j by PF1 (W_j ∈ NC_{m+1}); hence W_j − V_j − homot_m(φ_j, id, ∂W_j) = ∂H_j;
   (4c) since W_j is IM, V_j and H_j are IM.
5. (Bounds; PF4 with Λ := Λ_j, F := φ_j, G := id, and δ, using dist(φ_j(x), id(x)) ≤ δ on spt W_j, spt D_j, spt Z_j.)
   (5a) M(V_j) ≤ Λ_j^{m+1}M(W_j) ≤ (2Λ_j)^{m+1}M(W_j); M(Y_j) ≤ Λ_j^m M(D_j) ≤ (2Λ_j)^m M(D_j); M(L′_j) ≤ (2Λ_j)^m M(Z_j); M(H_j) ≤ δ(2Λ_j)^{m+1}M(W_j); M(E′_j) ≤ δ(2Λ_j)^m M(D_j); M(K_j) ≤ δ(2Λ_j)^m M(Z_j) (δ read as ENNReal.ofReal δ; Λ_j ≤ 2Λ_j, pow_le_pow_left). Write Σ_W := Σ_j (2Λ_j)^{m+1}M(W_j) < ∞ and Σ_D := Σ_j (2Λ_j)^m M(D_j) < ∞. Then Σ_j M(V_j) ≤ Σ_W, Σ_j M(H_j) ≤ δ·Σ_W, Σ_j M(Y_j) ≤ Σ_D and Σ_j M(E′_j) ≤ δ·Σ_D, all finite (ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum, ENNReal.tsum_mul_left, ENNReal.mul_lt_top).
   (5b) M(L′_N) → 0 and M(K_N) → 0 as N → ∞: they are bounded by (2Λ_N)^m M(Z_N) → 0 and δ·(2Λ_N)^m M(Z_N) → δ·0 = 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul, δ ≠ ∞), and squeezed below by 0.
   (5c) If x ∈ spt W_j then x ∈ A and dist(φ_j(x), x) ≤ δ, so φ_j(x) ∈ cthickening(δ, A) (mem_cthickening_of_dist_le) and φ_j(x) ∈ L; for y = φ_j(x) + t(x − φ_j(x)) with t ∈ [0, 1], y − x = (1 − t)(φ_j(x) − x), so dist(y, x) = (1 − t)·dist(φ_j(x), x) ≤ δ and y ∈ cthickening(δ, A). Hence spt V_j ⊆ φ_j(spt W_j) ⊆ L ∩ cthickening(δ, A) and spt H_j ⊆ cthickening(δ, A). Likewise (spt D_j ⊆ A') spt Y_j ⊆ φ_j(spt D_j) ⊆ cthickening(δ, A') and spt E′_j ⊆ cthickening(δ, A').

IMS with k := m and (V_j) (Σ M(V_j) < ∞) gives Q₀ ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}: HasSum (V_j(ω)) (Q₀(ω)) for every ω; M(Q₀) ≤ Σ_j M(V_j) ≤ Σ_W; spt Q₀ ⊆ closure ⋃_j spt V_j ⊆ L ∩ cthickening(δ, A), the latter set being closed (L closed, isClosed_cthickening; closure_minimal); Q₀ IM by (4c). Provenance: Simon Ch. 6, the remark preceding 4.10 (an increasing function of t is differentiable for L¹-a.e. t and the integral of its derivative over [a, b] is at most its increment). This is Lebesgue's theorem for monotone functions. In Mathlib its interval-integral form is MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv together with MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc (Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.DerivIntegrable, imported in the accepted Submission). Here deriv F is Mathlib's derivative, which is 0 wherever F is not differentiable.
1. (Empty interval.) If b ≤ a then Ioo a b = ∅ (Set.Ioo_eq_empty). The measure volume.restrict ∅ is 0 (Measure.restrict_empty), so the left side is 0 (lintegral_zero_measure), which is ≤ the right side. Assume from now on a < b.
2. (Nonnegativity.) Because F is monotone, deriv F t ≥ 0 for every t ∈ ℝ (Monotone.deriv_nonneg).
3. (Integrability.) F is monotone on uIcc a b (Monotone.monotoneOn), so deriv F is interval integrable on a..b (MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv). Since a ≤ b, this is IntegrableOn (deriv F) (Ioc a b) (intervalIntegrable_iff_integrableOn_Ioc_of_le). Hence IntegrableOn (deriv F) (Ioo a b) (IntegrableOn.mono_set with Ioo_subset_Ioc_self).
4. (Lower integral equals the real integral.) Apply ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal to the measure volume.restrict (Ioo a b), using steps 2 and 3: ∫⁻_{(a,b)} ofReal(deriv F t) dt = ofReal(∫_{(a,b)} deriv F t dt). Since ofReal is monotone (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal), it suffices to prove ∫_{(a,b)} deriv F ≤ F(b) − F(a).
5. (Conversion to an interval integral.) Lebesgue measure has no atoms, so ∫_{Ioo a b} deriv F = ∫_{Ioc a b} deriv F (integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo, read right to left). Since a ≤ b, ∫_{Ioc a b} deriv F = ∫_a^b deriv F (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le, read right to left).
6. (Lebesgue's bound.) Apply MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc to F, which is monotone on uIcc a b: ∫_a^b deriv F ∈ uIcc 0 (F(b) − F(a)). Since a ≤ b, monotonicity gives F(a) ≤ F(b), so 0 ≤ F(b) − F(a) and uIcc 0 (F(b) − F(a)) = Icc 0 (F(b) − F(a)) (Set.uIcc_of_le). Hence ∫_a^b deriv F ≤ F(b) − F(a), which by steps 4–5 is the claim. ∎

deriv F ≥ 0 everywhere (Monotone.deriv_nonneg), and deriv F is integrable on (a, b) (MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv, restricted from Ioc to Ioo).
